questions.stem: This diagram shows the microscopic organization of the granuloma of sarcoidosis, with a central core of epithelioid macrophages and a giant cell surrounded by a rim of lymphocytes. What key feature distinguishes this granuloma from that of tuberculosis?

explanation.summary: Sarcoid granulomas are non-caseating (no central necrosis), which helps distinguish them from the caseating granulomas of tuberculosis; they are compact collections of epithelioid macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, and a surrounding lymphocyte cuff.

questions.stem: Three endothelial architectures are compared. Which of the labeled types permits the freest passage of cells and large plasma proteins between blood and tissue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A capillary with intact intercellular tight junctions

choices.label: D
choices.text: A capillary relying only on transcytotic vesicles

explanation.summary: Sinusoidal capillaries have large fenestrations and intercellular gaps with a discontinuous basement membrane, allowing cells and large proteins to pass; continuous capillaries are least permeable and fenestrated ones are intermediate.
